clue.text: What's spent in Hungary on first goulash?

indicators.note: a goulash is a stew of mixed-up ingredients, so the letters of the preceding words are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A diner in Budapest spends money on a first course of goulash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goulash' looks like part of the Hungarian scene, but it is the anagram signal working on ON FIRST.
explanation.definitionFit: The forint is the national currency unit of Hungary, so forints are the money spent there.

clue.text: Imagined whim about nice soup

indicators.note: about means the word for whim goes round the other letters

parts.note: a fad is a passing whim or craze

indicators.note: in the soup means in a mess, so the letters of nice are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone dreamt up a sudden craving for a nice bowl of soup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soup' (as in 'in the soup', a mess) jumbles the second word into ANCIE, and 'about' wraps the craze round it; 'soup' looks like the thing being fancied.
explanation.definitionFit: To have fancied something is to have pictured it in the mind, a synonym of imagined.

clue.text: A flight that is an unchallenged success?

definitions.text: A flight that is an unchallenged success?

parts.words: A flight that is an unchallenged success?
parts.note: read as an escape, a flight that nobody stopped; read in sporting terms, a win so easy the loser never got near

explanation.surface: An escape that went off without anyone challenging it.
explanation.walkthrough: A runaway is one who takes flight, and a runaway win is one by a huge margin, so the clue plays on both senses.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-sided win in which the opponent never threatened is called a runaway result, a walkover.

clue.text: The game the Muses had to fasten their clothes?

parts.note: in Greek myth there were nine Muses
pins are used to hold clothes together

explanation.surface: A whimsical picture of the nine Muses pinning up their robes.
explanation.walkthrough: Ninepins is the old skittles game in which a ball is bowled at nine wooden pins.
explanation.definitionFit: Ninepins is a bowling pastime, a form of skittles, so it is a game.

clue.text: Document needed for bringing forward a match

definitions.text: Document needed for bringing forward a match

parts.words: Document needed for bringing forward a match
parts.note: the match is a marriage, and the paper is the permit that lets a wedding go ahead sooner than the usual notice allows

explanation.surface: Paperwork required to move a sports fixture to an earlier date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'match' suggests sport but means a marriage. In England a special licence lets a couple marry without the usual waiting period for banns.
explanation.definitionFit: This licence is an official permit from church authorities for a wedding to take place quickly or in an unusual place.

clue.text: Like cordage that is thick and poor in quality

explanation.surface: Describing a heavy rope that is also shoddily made.
explanation.walkthrough: Ropy is everyday British slang for poor or unwell, as in feeling a bit ropy.
explanation.definitionFit: Ropy describes something stringy and viscous, like rope, and in informal British use also means shoddy or in poor condition.

clue.text: Flat in a French street and what it may bring in?

indicators.note: in means the word for flat is placed inside the French street

parts.note: rue is French for street
even means flat or level

explanation.surface: An apartment on a Paris street, and the rent it might earn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flat' reads as an apartment, which is where the definition seems to lie, but it means level, EVEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Revenue is income, money that something earns for its owner.

clue.text: See 3
Inferior place of detention unsuitable for a light sentence

definitions.text: Inferior place of detention unsuitable for a light sentence

parts.words: Inferior place of detention unsuitable for a light sentence
parts.note: inferior here means lower down, an underground prison, and its darkness makes it no place for a light, that is short, term

explanation.surface: A grim jail that would be too harsh for someone with a short sentence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inferior' means lying below, and 'light' plays on both a mild sentence and daylight, which an underground cell lacks.
explanation.definitionFit: A dungeon is a dark prison cell, usually underground beneath a castle.

clue.text: The chosen way of life of the professional fighter?

definitions.text: The chosen way of life of the professional fighter?

parts.words: The chosen way of life of the professional fighter?
parts.note: a professional fighter is read as a serving soldier, whose chosen path in life is the armed forces

explanation.surface: Asking what path a prizefighter decided to follow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'professional fighter' suggests a boxer, but a soldier fights for a living too.
explanation.definitionFit: A life spent serving in the armed forces is a soldier's chosen profession.

clue.text: Policy pursued by the government that wanted to avoid trouble?

definitions.text: Policy pursued by the government that wanted to avoid trouble?

parts.words: Policy pursued by the government that wanted to avoid trouble?
parts.note: a state keeping out of other countries' conflicts in order to stay out of trouble

explanation.surface: A cautious government that keeps its head down.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is often linked with Britain and France refusing to intervene in the Spanish Civil War.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the policy of a state not meddling in the affairs or wars of other states.

clue.text: A War Office unit put back in the Middle West

indicators.note: put back means the whole string of pieces is written in reverse order

parts.note: WO is the abbreviation for the War Office, the former British ministry of the army
I, the Roman numeral one, stands for a unit

explanation.surface: A military unit being posted back to the American Midwest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put back' turns AWOI round as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: Iowa is a state in the American Midwest, the region also called the Middle West.

clue.text: US soldier, a s six-footer much above the average size

parts.note: GI is the usual name for an American soldier
an ant is an insect, and insects have six legs

explanation.surface: An American soldier over six feet tall, far bigger than most.
explanation.walkthrough: 'six-footer' suggests a tall person but means a creature with six feet.
explanation.definitionFit: A giant is a person or thing of huge size, far beyond the normal.

clue.text: It's illegal to have more than one, but I get involved with few anyway

definitions.text: It's illegal to have more than one

indicators.note: the letter I mixes in with the letters of few, so the combined letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A remark that bigamy is a crime, but the speaker carries on with several women regardless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get involved with' rearranges I and FEW; 'anyway' just rounds off the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Bigamy laws make it a crime to be married to more than one spouse at a time.

clue.text: He'd turn round at the end inevitably

indicators.note: turn round means the letters of the words that follow it are shifted into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone would come back around in the end, as they always do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn round' rearranges the first word and 'at' together. 'the end' looks like a time phrase, but with 'inevitably' it defines the end that comes to everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: Dying is the one ending that no living thing can escape.

clue.text: Begin drawing on a pavement, for example?

indicators.note: on means the drawing comes next, attached after the street

parts.note: ST, street, is the road of which a pavement forms a part
drawing is a form of art

explanation.surface: A pavement artist starting a chalk picture.
explanation.definitionFit: To start is to set something going, the same as to commence.

clue.text: A torch refill that is much better than 7?

definitions.text: A torch refill that is much better than 7?

parts.words: A torch refill that is much better than 7?
parts.note: the torch takes a battery, and 7, the answer to 7 down, is a damp underground cell, which a dry one beats

explanation.surface: A new battery for a flashlight that outperforms another kind.
explanation.walkthrough: A torch is the British word for a flashlight. The clue plays on cell as a battery and as a prison room: a dry one beats a damp dungeon.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a battery whose electrolyte is a paste rather than a liquid, the kind used in torches.

clue.text: What a patron of B R may do with his ticket

definitions.text: What a patron of B R may do with his ticket

parts.words: What a patron of B R may do with his ticket
parts.note: a customer of British Rail, holding a ticket, gets on board

explanation.surface: A rail customer deciding what to do with a ticket.
explanation.walkthrough: BR is British Rail, the former national railway of Britain; a ticket holder boards the train.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrain is to board a railway carriage, the natural next step for a passenger.

clue.text: The city whose milk is not TT

definitions.text: The city whose milk is not TT

parts.words: The city whose milk is not TT
parts.note: TT means teetotal, and this city's milk is a famous sweet sherry, so it is anything but alcohol-free

explanation.surface: A city whose dairy herds are not tuberculin-tested.
explanation.walkthrough: TT on British milk once meant tuberculin-tested, from cows certified free of tuberculosis, but it also means teetotal. Bristol Milk is a brand of cream sherry.
explanation.definitionFit: The English port city in the West Country gave its name to Bristol Milk sherry.

clue.text: Pernicious embargo on pro processed fuel

indicators.note: in a down answer on means the ban sits above the rearranged fuel

parts.note: a ban is an embargo or prohibition

indicators.note: processed means the letters of fuel are treated and turned into a new order

explanation.surface: A harmful ban on refined fuel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'processed' rearranges FUEL to EFUL, set under BAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Baneful means harmful or destructive, a near synonym of pernicious.

clue.text: See 4
Continue to deceive one's 12, maybe?

explanation.surface: Go on cheating on one's wife.
explanation.walkthrough: 12 is the answer to 12 across, a spouse.
explanation.definitionFit: To carry on is to keep going; it also means to have an affair, which is how a husband would betray a wife.

clue.text: Involved with cards he came badly to grief

indicators.note: the letters of cards are bound up with those of he and rearranged together

explanation.surface: A gambler lost heavily at the card table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Involved with' mixes CARDS and HE.
explanation.definitionFit: To have crashed is to have come to grief, like a car smash or a ruined venture.

clue.text: An off-day when Apollo rides high?

definitions.text: An off-day when Apollo rides high?

parts.words: An off-day when Apollo rides high?
parts.note: an off day is a day of no on, and the sun god Apollo is highest in the sky at midday

explanation.surface: A bad day for the Greek god of the sun.
explanation.walkthrough: Off is the opposite of on, so an off-day becomes a 'no-on' day; Apollo drives the sun's chariot, highest at midday.
explanation.definitionFit: The middle of the day, when the sun is at its highest point, is midday.

clue.text: Inane Old Testament comment

annotationWithheld.why: Inane Old Testament comment (4): the parse puts OT inside NE, both taken from 'Inane' read as 'In a NE', so 'Inane' is the container indicator and the letters N E at once

clue.text: King Charles described by Dr Johnson? Get away with you!

indicators.note: described by means the king's letters are drawn round by the doctor's name, sitting inside it

parts.note: Samuel Johnson, the dictionary writer, is Sam
CR stands for Carolus Rex, Latin for King Charles

explanation.surface: Dr Johnson's dictionary entry on King Charles, then an order to leave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'described' is used in its old geometric sense of drawn round, as a circle is described about a point; Carolus Rex is how King Charles signed himself.
explanation.definitionFit: Scram is a curt order to go away at once.

clue.text: Perfectly good type of headlight

parts.note: the light round the head of a perfectly good person, a saint in a painting

explanation.surface: A car headlamp that works fine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'headlight' suggests a car lamp but means a light round someone's head.
explanation.definitionFit: Saints in religious art are shown with a ring of light around the head.

clue.text: Hellish fluency

parts.note: fluency taken literally as a flowing, and the flowing is a river of the underworld

explanation.walkthrough: Fluency is read as flow, a river; in Greek myth the souls of the dead are ferried across it into Hades.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth this is the river bounding the underworld.

clue.text: But they don't do the crawl when swimming!

definitions.text: But they don't do the crawl when swimming!

parts.words: But they don't do the crawl when swimming!
parts.note: small water creatures that crawl on land, but in the water they swim by wriggling, not with the swimming stroke

explanation.surface: A remark about swimmers who avoid front crawl.
explanation.walkthrough: Newts crawl on land, but 'the crawl' is also the swimming stroke, which they do not use in water.
explanation.definitionFit: Young newts, which crawl about on land and swim in ponds, are called efts.

clue.text: What the inventor of the plough was?

definitions.text: What the inventor of the plough was?

parts.words: What the inventor of the plough was?
parts.note: the first person to plough a field was literally the first one out in it

explanation.surface: Asking about the person who first invented the plough.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase means the earliest in an area of activity; the inventor of the plough was literally first in a field.
explanation.definitionFit: To be the earliest to arrive in an area of activity is to be a pioneer there.

clue.text: It turns cross when beer is about

indicators.note: is about means the beer goes round the cross

parts.note: ale is a kind of beer
X is the shape of a cross

explanation.surface: Someone gets angry when beer is around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' reads as angry but is the letter X.
explanation.definitionFit: An axle is the rod on which a wheel rotates.

clue.text: Ruin some French classical city

parts.note: des is French for some
Troy is the ancient city of Greek legend

explanation.surface: A French phrase about an ancient city in ruins.
explanation.definitionFit: To destroy is to wreck, the same as to ruin.
